reviewNote: Checked on 2026-10-13. Routes lamanite-mission, missouri-1831, return-1831, missouri-1832, return-1832, canada-1833, canada-1833-return, recruiting-1834, zions-camp, and zions-camp-michigan: stops compared with the Joseph Smith Papers travel maps, which were opened and read. Routes jackson-expulsion, to-liberty-jail, missouri-exodus, and to-carthage: each stop is on a Joseph Smith Papers regional map that was opened and read; those maps draw no travel lines. The discharge site of the Camp of Israel was placed from the grid of the Northwest Missouri map, so it is approximate. Route kirtland-to-far-west: the dates, Norton, and Terre Haute come from a web search summary of Joseph Smith Papers pages; the pages were not read in full. Route salem-1836: the dates, New York City, and Boston come from a web search summary of Joseph Smith Papers pages; Buffalo and Albany were not checked. Routes new-york-to-ohio and colesville-branch: Fairport, Wellsville, and the river way come from a web search summary of Church history manuals; the arrival at Kaw Township on 26 July 1831 was read from the Church essay “The Journey of the Colesville Branch”. Routes across-iowa and pioneer-company: Council Bluffs, Winter Quarters, Fort Laramie, Fort Bridger, and the arrival on 24 July 1847 were read from Church history map 6; Sugar Creek, Garden Grove, Mount Pisgah, and South Pass were not checked. Route harmony-to-fayette was not checked against a source outside the section pages. Each `evidence` text tells the reader which of these applies.

upper-sandusky: Wyandot lands near Upper Sandusky, Ohio
camp-discharge: Camp discharge site, Clay County, Missouri

routes.title: Joseph and Oliver move from Harmony to Fayette
routes.summary: Opposition near Harmony led David Whitmer to bring Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery to his father's farm at Fayette. Translation was finished there in June 1829.
routes.evidence: Narrated move; direct line

routes.title: Mission to the Lamanites
routes.summary: Oliver Cowdery, Parley P. Pratt, Peter Whitmer Jr., and Ziba Peterson left New York in October 1830. They stopped near Kirtland, visited the Wyandot in Ohio, and reached the Missouri border in January 1831.
routes.evidence: Stops follow the Joseph Smith Papers map; the line between them is simplified

routes.title: The New York Saints gather to Ohio
routes.summary: Sections 37 and 38 command the New York members to gather to Ohio. Joseph and Emma Smith arrived in Kirtland about 1 February 1831; most branches followed by May. They went by the Erie Canal to Buffalo and by ship on Lake Erie to Fairport.
routes.evidence: The canal, Buffalo, and Fairport follow Church history manuals; one line stands for three branches

routes.title: The Colesville Branch moves to Thompson, then Missouri
routes.summary: The Colesville Saints settled at Thompson, Ohio, in May 1831. When the land arrangement there failed, section 54 sent them on to Missouri. They left Thompson in early June and went by steamboat from Wellsville, Ohio. They reached Kaw Township, Jackson County, on 26 July 1831.
routes.evidence: Wellsville and the river way follow Church history manuals. Cincinnati, Louisville, and Cairo mark the river, not known stops. Independence stands for Kaw Township

routes.title: Elders travel to Missouri, summer 1831
routes.summary: Section 52 sent elders in pairs to Missouri. Joseph Smith's party went by canal and river to St. Louis, then walked west to Independence in July 1831.
routes.evidence: Joseph Smith's party, with stops from the Joseph Smith Papers map; other pairs took different roads

routes.title: Return journey down the Missouri River
routes.summary: In August 1831 Joseph Smith and ten elders started home by canoe on the Missouri River. After danger at McIlwaine's Bend (section 61), most went on by land. They met other elders at Chariton (section 62) and reached Kirtland late in August.
routes.evidence: Places named in sections 60–62; the way home agrees with the Joseph Smith Papers map; later legs simplified

routes.title: Joseph Smith visits Missouri, spring 1832
routes.summary: Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Newel K. Whitney traveled to Independence in April 1832 to organize the Church's business and care for the poor (sections 78, 82, 83).
routes.evidence: Stops follow the Joseph Smith Papers map; river route simplified

routes.title: Return from Missouri, 1832
routes.summary: Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Newel K. Whitney left Independence by stagecoach on 6 May 1832. Near New Albany, Indiana, Whitney broke his leg in a stage accident. Rigdon went on to Ohio. Joseph Smith stayed with Whitney at Greenville, Indiana, for several weeks. The two men were back in Kirtland by the end of June.
routes.evidence: Stops follow the Joseph Smith Papers map; dates follow the Joseph Smith Papers introduction to the letter to Emma Smith, 6 June 1832. The day of arrival is not known

routes.title: Mission to Upper Canada
routes.summary: Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon left Kirtland in October 1833. Section 100 came at Perrysburg, New York; they then preached at Mount Pleasant, Upper Canada. From there they also went to Brantford, Waterford, and Colborne.
routes.evidence: Stops follow the Joseph Smith Papers map; lines simplified

routes.title: Return from Upper Canada
routes.summary: Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon went home from Mount Pleasant by way of Buffalo. They reached Kirtland in November 1833.
routes.evidence: Stops follow the Joseph Smith Papers map; lines simplified

routes.title: Recruiting mission to western New York
routes.summary: Section 103 called for men and money to help the Saints driven from Jackson County. In early 1834 Joseph Smith and Parley P. Pratt went from Kirtland to western New York to find recruits and funds. They went as far as the Avon area, then returned to Kirtland.
routes.evidence: Outbound stops follow the Joseph Smith Papers map; the return is not drawn

routes.title: Saints driven from Jackson County
routes.summary: In November 1833 armed residents drove about 1,200 Latter-day Saints from Jackson County. Most crossed the Missouri River north into Clay County.
routes.evidence: Forced move; Liberty stands for Clay County

routes.title: Camp of Israel (Zion's Camp)
routes.summary: Section 103 called for men to go to Zion's aid. About 200 volunteers marched from Ohio in May 1834. Section 105 came at Fishing River in June and told them not to fight. The camp was discharged soon after, near Liberty.
routes.evidence: Kirtland group. Stops follow the Joseph Smith Papers maps, plus Jacksonville; the discharge site is approximate; route simplified

routes.title: Camp of Israel: the Michigan group
routes.summary: Hyrum Smith and Lyman Wight recruited a second group in Michigan Territory. It left Pontiac on 5 May 1834. It joined the Kirtland group at the Salt River settlement in Missouri on 8 June 1834.
routes.evidence: Stops and dates follow the Joseph Smith Papers map; the line between them is simplified

routes.title: Journey to Salem, Massachusetts
routes.summary: Joseph Smith, Hyrum Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Oliver Cowdery left Kirtland on 25 July 1836, partly hoping to raise money for Church debts. They went by New York City and Boston and reached Salem on 5 August. Section 111 came there the next day.
routes.evidence: Dates, New York City, and Boston follow the Joseph Smith Papers. Buffalo and Albany are not checked; route simplified

routes.title: Joseph Smith moves from Kirtland to Far West
routes.summary: Joseph Smith left Kirtland on 12 January 1838 amid dissent and lawsuits. He waited at Norton, Ohio, for his family. The party went on by Terre Haute, Indiana, and reached Far West, Missouri, on 14 March 1838.
routes.evidence: Dates, Norton, and Terre Haute follow the Joseph Smith Papers; other stops are not known to us; lines simplified

routes.title: Joseph Smith taken to Liberty Jail
routes.summary: After the Saints surrendered at Far West in November 1838, Joseph Smith and other leaders were held at Independence and Richmond. In December they were sent to the jail at Liberty.
routes.evidence: Places of custody, in order

routes.title: Saints leave Missouri for Illinois
routes.summary: Under Governor Boggs's expulsion order, thousands of Saints left Missouri in the winter of 1838–39. Many found refuge at Quincy, Illinois, then settled at Commerce, later Nauvoo.
routes.evidence: Main refuge and settlement; families took many roads

routes.title: Joseph and Hyrum Smith go to Carthage
routes.summary: Joseph and Hyrum Smith went to Carthage in June 1844 to answer charges and were held in the county jail. A mob killed them there on 27 June 1844.
routes.evidence: Narrated journey

routes.title: Across Iowa to Winter Quarters
routes.summary: The Saints began leaving Nauvoo in February 1846 under threat of violence. They crossed Iowa, set up way stations, and wintered on the Missouri River.
routes.evidence: Council Bluffs and Winter Quarters follow the Church history map of the move west. Sugar Creek, Garden Grove, and Mount Pisgah are not checked; trails varied

routes.title: The vanguard company goes west
routes.summary: Section 136 organized the companies for the trek. Brigham Young's vanguard company left in April 1847 and reached the Salt Lake Valley in July.
routes.evidence: Fort Laramie and Fort Bridger follow the Church history map of the move west. South Pass is not checked; trail simplified
